_comment: prevent_self_review is false on purpose. This repo has one maintainer;
GitHub will not let a user approve their own deployment, so true would
make the prd gate permanently unsatisfiable.
deployment_branch_policy stays null (any branch may deploy). The main
ruleset is enforcing now, so protected_branches:true would finally be
accepted — but it would break PR plans. cd.yml plans on feature branches
using environment: val-readonly, and a feature branch is not protected,
so every PR plan would be refused a credential.
Four environments, not two. val-readonly and prd-readonly exist so a plan
runs as an identity that holds Reader and nothing else. They deliberately
have no reviewers: their whole purpose is to produce a plan *before*
anyone is asked to approve anything.
AZURE_CLIENT_ID is a variable, not a secret. Under OIDC a client ID
authorises nothing on its own — the federated subject does, and it names
this repository and one environment. Declaring it as a secret would also
make it unreadable in a diff for no benefit.
secrets stay empty. A declared-but-absent secret is a hard failure: the
API cannot create one without a value.
